Looks nice and that’s it. Don’t bother
Jan 2025 • Family
We went here for New Year’s Eve dinner at 6pm ish. A family of 6 we walked in and was taken to the first floor and shown to a table. On entry the ground floor and first floor I would say was 80% to capacity. 

From the outside the restaurant looks really nice inside it’s the same. Unfortunately the customer service and food doesn’t reflect this. We ordered starters first which took around 30 minutes, drinks took about the same time. Once we finished our starters we ordered mains. The waiter told us the food will take 1 hour. We were happy to wait, I would say 45 minutes in and the food started arriving. We had one dish which was a pizza which didn’t come to the table. After a hour I asked the waiter about the pizza and he told us he didn’t order it. His whole approach wasn’t apologetic just “it is what it is”. 

During our dinner there was lack of tissues, no one really came to the table to ask if we needed any more drinks and anything else. Clearing the table we had to ask 5 times. The whole experience was applauding and I would not recommend this restaurant. When we got our bill as someone else has mentioned about the hidden charges they are right. I told the waiter I’m not paying for the Service Charge and to remove it. Make sure you check your bills as they will charge you a service charge for drinks and separately for food so you are being ripped off. I made them take it off.

When paying the bill the lady downstairs took payment and asked about not paying service. I told her whilst the waiter was standing next to me but there was nothing put to me to make the situation right. I would stay clear of this restaurant and go somewhere else. If you do decide to dine here make sure you triple check your bill and good luck.

No culture shock - it's a comfortable coffee shop...
Sep 2011
You say you want to try new places, but the monsoonal rain of a Saigon summer can sap the pioneering spirit of even the most ardent adventurer... especially those intrepid few who brave District One. 

Literally around the corner from the better District One hotels, getting there inevitably offers the Western traveler the opportunity to pick up a newspaper from back home, and for probably a little cheaper than it goes for at your railway station newsstand back home too . 

As has been mentioned in other reviews, it is a cafe of three levels, each with a profoundly different character. This review deals only with the ground floor, of which we became daily patrons for breakfasts that stretched into lunch. 

Look for the booths on the far side of the cafe, which afford both lounging and privacy. The tables and chairs in the main area though offer street views.

You won't, or at least we didn't, find the place bouncing with backpackers or overrun with tourists. It's mainly middle class locals there for the same things. To read a newspaper or chat with friends and colleagues over coffee and cake. 

There's some conversation in other reviews here too about the service. It wasn't by any means bad. And yes, staff were, well, young and fooled about a lot more than seemed appropriate. And while you probably don't see ice fights at Starbucks, it didn't come at the expense of my breakfast, which was excellent each day. 

In short - it's a very familiar french inspired coffee shop experience. 

There's no great culture shock, but it's not touristy either. 

Some tips, take the extra set of stairs to the toilets on the third floor. The top floor bar is uniquely funkified. 

Prices are totally reasonsonable for this part of town, remembering you're not in district 3.

The Ciao cafe is very clean and well presented. The three levels all have a different feel, the top level in particular is very funky. It's certainly inviting and a nice place to sit and people watch for a while.

The service is average at best. They have a lot of staff but they're not trained to survey the floor to see if anyone wants anything so it can take some effort to order or pay. Ciao, like most cafes in Saigon serve complimentary iced tea but at Ciao you have to ask for it and it has a unpleasantly strong taste.

The drinks are all good, as are the deserts. I've not had a meal but they look large and tasty.

The Ciao is well worth a visit but be patient with service.
